THIS BUMP IS ABOUT WHAT THE READING VIEW SERVES.

WHAT MEASURED IT, AND WHY NO GATE BEFORE THIS ONE SAW IT. A gate now simulates the reading view's own fold (tools/fold-probe.mjs): the reader applies every rule to every INLINE RUN it renders, plain substring, EVERY occurrence, in rule order (Reader/Document.elm applyCorrections). Every earlier gate measured the BLOCK domain instead (extract.mjs editReport — every block's own text, running heads and page markers included), so a rule whose find is not unique to the point it was written for rewrote every other point carrying the same text. MEASURED on 1.0.6, RENDERED with the committed bundle (happy-dom) over the LIVE /t: the served reading view read supermundaneessential, supermundanefull, supermundanemundane (x2) and four more compounds, and 'about unsure God' where the print reads 'about the first God'. The gate's scope assertion fails that state with 135 rules named, r11094 and r10934 among them; its own derivation of the fold domain is checked against the reader's rendering (2,543 of 2,543 paragraphs of this edition agree).

1. THE MULTI-FIRE RULES. 135 rules fire more than once IN THE READING VIEW (181 in the block domain). Each was decided on its own evidence; the split is 117 licensed "all", 8 flagged, 5 scoped by a context-unique find, 5 withdrawn:
   - 117 carry `scope: "all"` with a per-rule `scope_why`: the find is not a form the print sets at ANY occurrence. MEASURED against the human-proofread witness of the same print (Project Gutenberg 77393/78800, Distributed Proofreaders): the find's form occurs 0 times there while the rule's reading occurs (Timeeus 0 against Timaeus 259, firom 0 against from 4307, thp 0 against the 32057, and 80 such rules in all), or the mark it removes is one this print cannot set at that position (a doubled mark, a mark fused where the print sets a word boundary). The same defect is at every occurrence, so the rule repairs every one.
   - 8 carry `scope: "flagged"` with the evidence that would decide them — the find fires where the print's own text may stand and the re-flowed witness cannot say: r11168 ('with,' at 14 sites, where the transcription carries the same paired-comma construction elsewhere), r9102 and r9970 (a comma between a subject and its verb), r9496 and r11055 (a bracket that IS the print's own at some sites), r11207 (a legitimate closing quote before 'For'), r11222 (a bare asterisk, which in THIS print is the FOOTNOTE MARKER, at 26 sites), r11537 (a quote opening a quotation). Each names the evidence that would settle it: the punctuation-preserving page models of the two other ingested copies (sixbooksproclus00unkngoog, bub_gb_svwwAQAAMAAJ), which tools/witness-unsure.mjs already knows how to read.
   - 5 are scoped to the ONE site they were written for by extending the find to a context-unique string (the library's own unique-find discipline, tools/merge.mjs `widen`), each re-issued under a new id with the old one spent: r10934 'exempts' -> 'is exempts from' (the witness carries the print's own 'exempts' at the other three sites), r9794 'the replenishes of' -> 'the replenishers of' ('which replenishes intelligence' is the print's own verb), r11472 'three son! of' -> 'three sons of' ('O son!' is the print's own exclamation mark), r11426 'For the* which each' -> 'For that which each' (the witness reads 'that' at exactly ONE of the seven sites and 'the' at the other six, which keep the transcription's own characters with the '*' marked as damage), r9926 'suspended from, their' -> 'suspended from their' (the next site is a paired-comma construction the print may set).
   - 5 are WITHDRAWN WITH NO REPLACEMENT, and 4 of them are a CROSS-CLASS FINDING reported for the unit that owns the wrong-reading class: the human-proofread witness reads OUR FIND verbatim at every site the rule fires at, so the rule serves a reading the print does not have — r9550 ('one or being' -> 'one and being'; the witness reads 'the one or being' at BOTH sites), r8942 ('beings themselves' -> 'being itself'; the witness reads 'beings themselves' at all three, and the rule's own rationale says 'print likely reads' — a guess), r10812 ('honored' -> 'honoured'; the witness reads 'honored' at both, the print's own spelling), r9707 ('uncoarranged' -> 'unco-arranged'; the witness reads 'uncoarranged' at both and 'unco-arranged' never). The FIFTH is r11094 ('super-' -> 'supermundane'): the print sets 'super-' at the foot of page 153 and 'mundane' at the head of page 154 — its OWN page-break hyphenation, with a footnote and a Greek quotation between them — and NO find/replace can join those two parts (they are not adjacent in the reading view's fold domain). Scoping the find to that one site — this unit's first attempt, and the reviewer's recommendation — made the reading view read 'the ruling supermundane' at the foot and 'mundane order' at the next page's head: the word TWICE. Withdrawn instead, so all nine occurrences of 'super-' serve the print's own text. The five old ids and the 31 ids the sentinel rules spent are recorded in tools/repair-id-probe.mjs.

2. THE 'unsure' SENTINEL IS GONE FROM THE DATA AND FROM THE VIEW. 31 rules recorded 'no reading is determinable here' by replacing their text with the English word 'unsure'. The reader has NO case for a sentinel, so it was served as prose — MEASURED, rendered: 12 times in the reading view (the other 172 firings are running-head blocks the view suppresses), three of them destroying real words ('about unsure God' for the print's 'about the first God', 'so Parmenides first unsure' for the fragment 'attri-', and a whole damaged critical note). r9908 drops the stray page digit as it was written to ('the 1 first' -> 'the first'), r8654 preserves the word fragment ('attri-Proc. Vol. I, 2 E' -> 'attri-'), and the other 29 replace with this edition's own DAMAGE CHARACTER, which the reading view ALREADY renders highlighted with the title 'damage in the transcription here — no reading is recorded for this word'. NO READER CHANGE WAS NEEDED, and the brief's premise is stated as refuted: the convention for this case exists in the reader (damageSpans), and the model's other route to it — \`action: "leave"\` with class 'review' — is UNREACHABLE here, because ids must ASCEND in rule order while classes must be GROUPED, so a review rule would have to sort after every reading rule and would break the id sequence. One narrow exemption was needed in the extractor's reading policy (extract.mjs checkReadingPolicy): a rule whose whole replacement is ONE damage character records a MARK, not a word, and the policy's question ('would the reading view assert a word the edition does not have?') has no word to answer for. It is stated narrowly for that reason; a rule that resolves a damaged word to an actual word is still caught.

3. THE MODEL'S OWN CONSEQUENCE, FOLLOWED TO A FIXED POINT. A changed reading is a NEW id, never an edit under a spent id (RULE_FIELDS in tools/repair-id-probe.mjs includes `after`). 36 rules were re-issued as r11857-r11894; TWO of those ids are spent with no rule, because at the end of the list an earlier rule consumes their find first and they stand in running-head blocks the reading view suppresses. Moving a rule to the end also frees the text it used to consume, so TWO carried rules fired a different number of times and were re-issued for that reason alone (r11022, r11059) — the cascade the model implies, run to a fixed point (second pass: 0 rewritten carried records, 0 dead rules).

MEASURED AFTER THE CHANGE, and every one of the 15 gates green by exit code: 3,255 rules (1.0.6: 3,262), every one fires at least once (checkEdits), 3,769 applications in the served text (1.0.6: 3,799); 0 rules fire more than once in the reading view without a licence; 0 rules serve a sentinel word; 191 rules fire only in blocks the reading view suppresses (1.0.6: 193); and NO RULE FIRES MORE THAN ONCE IN THE READING VIEW while more than 1,400 reach the served view at exactly one point each.
